input.question: Alright, so we all know most Hollywood films get history wrong, but are there any Hollywood blockbusters that are very historically accurate?
input.ground_truth: Master and Commander is both a really good movie, and actually historically accurate, to an extent. I've watched it, and I didn't see any particular inaccuracies about life onboard a wooden warship. The plot is based off of the British chase of the American commerce raider [U.S.S *Essex*](_URL_0_) during the War of 1812, which sailed down the eastern coast of Brazil, then up into the Pacific where it destroyed the British whaling industry. Of course, Americans don't want to see Americans as the bad guys in films, so they made the antagonist a French ship, but still.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Alright, so we all know most Hollywood films get history wrong, but are there any Hollywood blockbusters that are very historically accurate?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of building blocks. Some people build things that look cool but aren’t exactly how things were in real life—they add extra blocks or leave some out. That’s like when movies change history to make the story more fun or easier to understand.

But some movies try really, really hard to build things just like they were in real life. They use the right blocks in the right places. These movies try to show history the way it really happened. 

For example, the movie “Apollo 13” is about astronauts and tries very hard to show what really happened when their spaceship got in trouble. Another movie, “Schindler’s List,” also tries to show history as close to the real story as possible.

So, even though most movies play a little loose with history, a few try to be very careful and show things the way they really were.
